title: Retinol for Men: 7 Things You Need to Know
summary: Retinol is a powerful anti-aging ingredient for men. Learn how to use it correctly, what to expect, and the best tips for a smoother complexion.
body_markdown:
## How to use retinol for men


Retinol may be powerful, but the catch is that it isn’t so straightforward to use. Compared to other skincare products, retinol comes with certain rules, which if you don’t follow can cause side effects. Here’s what you need to do to reap the full benefits of retinol:


1. Use retinol at night


Retinol becomes less potent when exposed to the sun, so it should only be used at bedtime. As a general rule, active ingredients should be applied at night as this is when the skin renews itself. Reserve the daytime for products that protect your skin from environmental stressors and pollutants. For instance, you could use a vitamin C serum during the day and a retinol cream for men in the evening.


1. Start slow


Your skin won’t always give retinol a warm welcome, so the key is to slowly integrate it into your[skincare routine](https://www.provenskincare.com/blog/the-best-skincare-routine-for-men/) . Start using it only once or twice a week to see how your skin reacts, and then work your way up to every other night. You can incorporate retinol into your nightly routine, but only if you’ve fully built tolerance for it.


Are side effects normal? You might experience some side effects such as redness and dryness as your skin adapts to retinol. You might even go through the “retinol uglies”, which is when your skin purges. Don’t worry — it’s all part of the process. The side effects should subside once your skin has acclimated.


1. Start low


Retinol comes in various concentrations (0.01 to 1 percent). You may be tempted to start with the strongest concentration to get rid of the signs of aging ASAP, but that’s not a good idea. Starting with high-strength retinol can wreak havoc on your skin.


If you’ve never used retinol for men before or if you have sensitive skin, go for low-concentration retinol (0.01 to 0.03 percent) to give your skin time to get used to this ingredient. Remember, the best retinol for men isn’t always the most concentrated one — when it comes to retinol, a little can go a long way.


1. Apply retinol on dry skin


Some skincare products can be applied on damp skin, but not retinol. This is because retinol and retinoids will be absorbed more deeply into your skin when it’s wet. This may not be a problem for men who’ve built a tolerance for retinol, but it can be a cause for concern in men with sensitive skin.


1. Use hyaluronic acid


Combat the dryness that comes with retinol use by using hyaluronic acid, a substance that boosts the skin’s moisture content. Put on retinol first so the skin can soak it in, and only apply hyaluronic acid once the retinol has dried so you don’t reduce retinol’s potency. But if you have sensitive skin, hyaluronic acid can be applied first — that way, it can water down the retinol to make it more tolerable.


If you’re using a retinol cream for men, there’s a good chance that it already contains hyaluronic acid, so there’s no need to top it off with more moisture.


1. Be careful with combinations


Retinol for men works wonders but it doesn’t work well with other ingredients. Once you add retinol to your routine, you’re going to have to be very careful of your skincare pairings. For example, salicylic acid might be able to unclog your pores, but like retinol, it can also lead to[dry skin](https://www.provenskincare.com/blog/how-to-fix-dry-skin-patches/) . Combining it with retinol will put your skin at risk of being too dry. When this happens, your skin will ramp up its oil production and you’ll end up with more acne.


1. Wear sunscreen


Retinol makes your skin more sensitive to the sun. This means it’s more susceptible to sun damage such as sunburns, sun spots, and skin cancer. With that said, always wear a broad-spectrum[sunscreen with SPF](https://www.provenskincare.com/blog/what-is-spf-and-what-spf-should-you-use/) during the day,[reapply often](https://www.provenskincare.com/blog/how-often-should-you-reapply-sunscreen/) , and practice other sun safety tips.
